turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Of course. First, a worked example.
I work at home. Ali works at home. I ask: who is it? Ali is one person, so he. With he, I add -s: works.
Rule: after he, she or it, the verb takes -s.
Right: He walks to work every day. Wrong: He walk to work every day.

Your turn. Fill the gap with the verb only:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
turns.judgeInput:

W2 (wrong) strength 2: -s goes on every verb and -es/-ies are not needed. Its error: adds -s wrongly or misspells -es/-ies ("She watchs TV", "I plays").
C1 (correct) strength 1: add -s/-es after he/she/it. Independent correct productions so far: 0.

I work at home. → He works at home.
Step 1: I find the word before the verb: "he".
Step 2: "he" means I add -s, so "work" becomes "works".
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s to the verb.
Right: "She cooks every evening." Wrong: "She cook every evening."
